actor.description: Recorded actor identity, not host-authenticated authority.

file.description: A staged file relative to the work directory. The consumer verifies its actual bytes against sha256.

relativePath.description: A slash-separated file path relative to the work directory; no absolute path, dot segment, parent traversal, drive prefix or backslash.

context.description: Supporting notes and reference files used to understand the task, separate from its inputs. Empty collections explicitly mean no extra context. Context does not grant additional execution authority.
context.title: Request context

decision.description: .works/<workId>/decisions/<id>.json: an attributed decision on an exact work revision and subject digest. Identity and authority are not authenticated by this schema.
decision.title: Decision

evidence.description: .works/<workId>/evidence/<id>.json: artifact metadata. Existence, actual digest and evidentiary relevance require separate checks.
evidence.title: Evidence

index.description: Version 1 of the proposed .works document format. A document must match exactly one kind. This contract does not migrate or reinterpret legacy session records.
index.title: Works document contract

inputs.description: The prompts and files the request asks the skill to act on. At least one prompt or file is required.
inputs.title: Request inputs

output.description: One produced output. Text is inline; commits identify a repository and full object ID; images and other files bind persisted artifacts. Output metadata alone does not prove correctness or publication.
output.title: Response output

request.description: .works/<workId>/requests/<id>.json: prompts and files to act on, with supporting context kept separate, against one work revision. This record alone grants no execution permission.
request.title: Request

response.description: .works/<workId>/responses/<id>.json: typed outputs produced for one request. Optional verification observations describe their checks separately; delivering an output is not a claim that the work is proved complete.

feedbackRound.description: Completed feedback-and-repair rounds for this request. Initial candidate is round zero; the caller maintains truthful history.

response.title: Response

work.description: .works/<id>/work.json: goal, declared scope, acceptance criteria and current lifecycle.
work.title: Work

@cli/curl.purpose: Probe an HTTP endpoint using the curl executable.

@cli/docker.purpose: Inspect or operate containers and images through Docker CLI.

@cli/git.bind: Resolved executable path and reported version in the active environment; working directory and arguments declared by the invocation.
@cli/git.purpose: Inspect or change Git repository state.

@cli/python.bind: Resolved executable path and reported version in the active environment; working directory and arguments declared by the invocation.
@cli/python.note: Resolve Python 3 from the active environment: python, python3, or py -3 as appropriate; record the selected executable and any launcher arguments.

@remote/ghcr.purpose: A container image pinned by digest.

@remote/github-actions.bind: Repository identity, run id, head commit and observed conclusion.

@tools/fileread.bind: Capability advertised by the active session; availability and invocation permissions checked at use time.
@tools/fileread.purpose: Read declared workspace files and directories through the active session.

claude.via: Claude Code Read, Glob and Grep

@tools/print.bind: Capability advertised by the active session; availability and invocation permissions checked at use time.
@tools/print.purpose: Present text and artifacts in the conversation using the host rendering capabilities.

openai.via: the absolute path or the URL printed into the conversation, with the image inline where the client renders one

@tools/sourcewrite.bind: Capability advertised by the active session; availability and invocation permissions checked at use time.
@tools/sourcewrite.purpose: Edit files within the declared write scope through the active session.

@workspaces/artifacts.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/artifacts.purpose: Produced files, including images, documents and other deliverables.

@workspaces/context.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/context.purpose: Supporting reference files for a request.

@workspaces/inputs.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/inputs.purpose: Files supplied as the subject of a request.

@workspaces/requests.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/requests.purpose: Requests with separate inputs and context.

@workspaces/responses.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/responses.purpose: Responses declaring produced outputs and execution status.

criteria.stopWhen: Stop after two feedback rounds, repeated failed steady state, missing authorization, concurrent drift, exhausted recovery, unavailable rollback identity or unobservable uncertain effect. Never duplicate deploy effects.

purpose: Deploy one immutable release to one authorized target, observe bounded steady-state probes, and take only the declared recovery or exact-digest rollback branch when needed.

request.description: Bind passing quality evidence, immutable release and manifest digests, one target, existing deploy authorization, steady-state probes and deadline, exact rollback identity, and migration proof when required.
request.title: release.deploy request

response.description: A done response names the exact active digest, target revisions, authorization, branch taken and bounded observation series. A rollback result names the restored predecessor and is never described as a successful new deployment.
response.title: release.deploy response

scope: One release identity and target. Every effect is compare-and-set, credentials remain named references, production requires existing authorization, and uncertain effects are observed before any further mutation.

calls.purpose: Read release, authority and predecessor evidence.
Verify immutable source and manifest provenance.

steps.instruction: Read the exact request and declared evidence. Bind one immutable release and manifest digest, target, passing quality evidence, required migration proof, existing deploy authorization, probes, steady deadline, rollback identity and open coverage record. Production authorization must already exist.

calls.purpose: Read declared target and public probe state.

steps.instruction: Observe artifact availability, host, active digest, schema, domain, target revision and credential custody before effects. Classify each state reusable, missing, invalid, foreign or uncertain and record compare-and-set preconditions.

calls.purpose: Apply the authorized target rollout by immutable digest.
Persist attempted effects and compare-and-set revisions.

steps.instruction: Apply only approved compare-and-set preparation and rollout effects for the same immutable release. Record every attempted effect and its precondition. Never substitute an artifact, expand target scope or repeat an uncertain effect.

calls.purpose: Collect bounded health and readiness observations.

steps.instruction: Observe the active digest and timestamped health and readiness probes after rollout or an uncertain result. Detect a third-party release before any further action. Require fresh observation before retrying any effect.

calls.purpose: Apply one approved recovery action or exact-digest rollback.
calls.when: only on the authorized fallback branch

calls.purpose: Observe target state after each fallback action.
Persist each fallback observation and effect.

steps.instruction: Only after observed rollout failure, apply approved bounded reversible actions one at a time for the same release, observing after each. If exhausted, restore only the authorized rollback identity by exact digest after proving it exists and is data-compatible.
produces: Ordered recovery or rollback transcript when needed.

calls.purpose: Persist the deployment or rollback receipt from observed state.

steps.instruction: Compare authority, immutable identity, compare-and-set effects, active digest, observation window and fallback branch. Produce concrete defects. A rollback reports the predecessor restored and never claims the new release deployed.
produces: Concrete failed-criterion feedback or passing review results.

calls.purpose: Present the observed active state and probes.

steps.instruction: Write and validate the response with actual artifacts, observations and review results. Present healthy deployment only after steady state is proved; otherwise present the actual active state and failure.

validate.failurePolicy: Evaluate deployment evidence into concrete defects. Repair only within two feedback rounds, observe target state before every retry, and never duplicate deploy or rollback effects whose completion is uncertain.

review.instruction: Confirm existing authorization covers the project, environment, target and deploy action; quality and optional migration evidence bind the same immutable release and manifest digest.
Verify each host, artifact, schema, domain and rollout effect used observed before and after revisions, stayed within the one target, and did not repeat an uncertain mutation.

Check at least two timestamped health and readiness observations over the bounded window, including a public probe, prove the active digest, and reject a single successful sample or assumed stability.

Confirm rollout failure enters only approved reversible recovery for the same release; exhausted recovery enters exact-digest rollback; rollback compatibility and identity are proven before restoration.
Confirm no third release became active during execution. Any concurrent or uncertain state stops further effects until a fresh observation and authorization-bound plan exist.
